title: Sharing and Measuring: Fractions
seo_title: Fractions Class 4 Worksheet with Answers (Maths Mela Chapter 5)
standard_code: Class 4, Maths Mela Chapter 5: Sharing and Measuring
standard_text: Fractions: equal sharing, fractions of a whole and of a collection, equivalent fractions, and comparing fractions in measuring contexts (summary of NCERT Maths Mela Class 4)
meta_desc: Class 4 Sharing and Measuring worksheet (Maths Mela Chapter 5): fractions of shapes and amounts, equivalent fractions, comparing. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • To find 3/4 of 20, divide by 4 then multiply by 3: 15.
  • 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8: equivalent fractions name the same amount.

Examples

Example

Find 2/5 of 30.

30 ÷ 5 = 6

6 × 2

Answer: 12

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Dividing by the numeratorDivide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator.
Thinking 1/8 > 1/4Eighths are smaller pieces.

faq.a: Fractions that show the same amount, like 1/2 and 3/6.

faq.q: How do I find a fraction of a number?
faq.a: Divide by the bottom number, then multiply by the top number.

items.q:
The bars are the same size and show the same amount.
12 = ?4
items.e: The bottom bar has 4 equal parts, so each half of the top bar is split into 2 parts. 1 shaded half becomes 1 × 2 = 2 shaded parts. So 12 = 24.

items.q:
The bars are the same size and show the same amount.
13 = ?6
items.e: The bottom bar has 6 equal parts, so each third of the top bar is split into 2 parts. 1 shaded third becomes 1 × 2 = 2 shaded parts. So 13 = 26.

items.q:
The bars are the same size and show the same amount.
34 = ?8
items.e: The bottom bar has 8 equal parts, so each quarter of the top bar is split into 2 parts. 3 shaded quarters become 3 × 2 = 6 shaded parts. So 34 = 68.

items.q:
The bars are the same size and show the same amount.
25 = ?10
items.e: The bottom bar has 10 equal parts, so each fifth of the top bar is split into 2 parts. 2 shaded fifths become 2 × 2 = 4 shaded parts. So 25 = 410.

items.q:
The bars are the same size and show the same amount.
12 = ?8
items.e: The bottom bar has 8 equal parts, so each half of the top bar is split into 4 parts. 1 shaded half becomes 1 × 4 = 4 shaded parts. So 12 = 48.

items.q:
The bars are the same size and show the same amount.
23 = ?6
items.e: The bottom bar has 6 equal parts, so each third of the top bar is split into 2 parts. 2 shaded thirds become 2 × 2 = 4 shaded parts. So 23 = 46.

items.q:
The bars are the same size and show the same amount.
14 = ?8
items.e: The bottom bar has 8 equal parts, so each quarter of the top bar is split into 2 parts. 1 shaded quarter becomes 1 × 2 = 2 shaded parts. So 14 = 28.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 12 is shaded. How many eighths are equal to 12?
items.e: Look down the fraction wall. 12 lines up with 4 eighths, because each half is the same as 4 eighths. So 12 = 48.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 34 is shaded. How many eighths are equal to 34?
items.e: Look down the fraction wall. 34 lines up with 6 eighths, because each quarter is the same as 2 eighths. So 34 = 68.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 23 is shaded. How many sixths are equal to 23?
items.e: Look down the fraction wall. 23 lines up with 4 sixths, because each third is the same as 2 sixths. So 23 = 46.

items.q: What fraction of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: The rectangle has 10 equal parts, so the denominator (bottom number) is 10. 4 parts are shaded, so the numerator (top number) is 4. The answer is 410. The shaded parts do not need to be side by side.

items.q: What fraction of the rectangle is shaded?
items.e: The rectangle has 8 equal parts, so the denominator (bottom number) is 8. 6 parts are shaded, so the numerator (top number) is 6. The answer is 68. The shaded parts do not need to be side by side.

items.q: What fraction of the counters are green?
items.e: The whole is the set of 6 counters, so the denominator is 6. 2 are green: 26. Do not compare green with white (2 to 4).

items.q: What fraction of the counters are green?
items.e: The whole is the set of 8 counters, so the denominator is 8. 3 are green: 38. Do not compare green with white (3 to 5).

items.q: What fraction of the counters are green?
items.e: The whole is the set of 10 counters, so the denominator is 10. 4 are green: 410. Do not compare green with white (4 to 6).

items.q: What fraction of the counters are green?
items.e: The whole is the set of 5 counters, so the denominator is 5. 3 are green: 35. Do not compare green with white (3 to 2).

items.q: What fraction of the counters are not green?
items.e: There are 8 counters in the set. 5 are green, so 8 − 5 = 3 are not green. The answer is 38.

items.q: What fraction of the balls are big?
items.e: In a set, each object is one part, even if it is bigger. There are 4 balls and 1 is big: 14.

items.q: A bag has 5 red marbles and 3 blue marbles. What fraction of the marbles are blue?
items.e: The whole set is 5 + 3 = 8 marbles. 3 are blue, so 38 are blue. 35 compares blue with red; it does not use the whole set.

items.q: A box has 10 pencil crayons. 3 of them are broken. What fraction of the pencil crayons are broken?
items.e: There are 10 pencil crayons in the set and 3 are broken. So 310 are broken.

items.q: Find 15 of 30.
items.e: To find 15, divide by the denominator: 30 ÷ 5 = 6.

items.q: Find 13 of 21.
items.e: To find 13, divide by the denominator: 21 ÷ 3 = 7.

items.q: Find 14 of 28.
items.e: To find 14, divide by the denominator: 28 ÷ 4 = 7.

items.q: Find 16 of 42.
items.e: To find 16, divide by the denominator: 42 ÷ 6 = 7.

items.q: Find 18 of 40.
items.e: To find 18, divide by the denominator: 40 ÷ 8 = 5.

items.q: What is 14 of 36?
items.e: To find 14, divide by the denominator: 36 ÷ 4 = 9.

items.q: What is 17 of 35?
items.e: To find 17, divide by the denominator: 35 ÷ 7 = 5.

items.q: What is 110 of 60?
items.e: To find 110, divide by the denominator: 60 ÷ 10 = 6.

items.q: What is 19 of 54?
items.e: To find 19, divide by the denominator: 54 ÷ 9 = 6.

items.q: What is 112 of 48?
items.e: To find 112, divide by the denominator: 48 ÷ 12 = 4.

items.q: Find 34 of 24.
items.e: First find 14: 24 ÷ 4 = 6. Then multiply by the numerator: 6 × 3 = 18.

items.q: Find 25 of 30.
items.e: First find 15: 30 ÷ 5 = 6. Then multiply by the numerator: 6 × 2 = 12.

items.q: Find 23 of 18.
items.e: First find 13: 18 ÷ 3 = 6. Then multiply by the numerator: 6 × 2 = 12.

items.q: Find 56 of 36.
items.e: First find 16: 36 ÷ 6 = 6. Then multiply by the numerator: 6 × 5 = 30.

items.q: Find 38 of 40.
items.e: First find 18: 40 ÷ 8 = 5. Then multiply by the numerator: 5 × 3 = 15.

items.q: What is 25 of 35 cm?
items.e: First find 15: 35 ÷ 5 = 7 cm. Then multiply by the numerator: 7 cm × 2 = 14 cm.

items.q: What is 34 of 1,000 g?
items.e: First find 14: 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 g. Then multiply by the numerator: 250 g × 3 = 750 g.

items.q: What is 47 of 63?
items.e: First find 17: 63 ÷ 7 = 9. Then multiply by the numerator: 9 × 4 = 36.

items.q: What is 58 of 48?
items.e: First find 18: 48 ÷ 8 = 6. Then multiply by the numerator: 6 × 5 = 30.

items.q: What is 310 of 90 mL?
items.e: First find 110: 90 ÷ 10 = 9 mL. Then multiply by the numerator: 9 mL × 3 = 27 mL.

items.q: 34 = ?12
items.e: Look at the denominators: 4 × 3 = 12. Multiply the numerator by 3 too: 3 × 3 = 9. So 34 = 912.

items.q: 23 = ?9
items.e: Look at the denominators: 3 × 3 = 9. Multiply the numerator by 3 too: 2 × 3 = 6. So 23 = 69.

items.q: 25 = ?15
items.e: Look at the denominators: 5 × 3 = 15. Multiply the numerator by 3 too: 2 × 3 = 6. So 25 = 615.

items.q: 56 = ?12
items.e: Look at the denominators: 6 × 2 = 12. Multiply the numerator by 2 too: 5 × 2 = 10. So 56 = 1012.

items.q: 38 = ?16
items.e: Look at the denominators: 8 × 2 = 16. Multiply the numerator by 2 too: 3 × 2 = 6. So 38 = 616.

items.q: 13 = ?12
items.e: Look at the denominators: 3 × 4 = 12. Multiply the numerator by 4 too: 1 × 4 = 4. So 13 = 412.

items.q: 45 = ?20
items.e: Look at the denominators: 5 × 4 = 20. Multiply the numerator by 4 too: 4 × 4 = 16. So 45 = 1620.

items.q: 37 = ?14
items.e: Look at the denominators: 7 × 2 = 14. Multiply the numerator by 2 too: 3 × 2 = 6. So 37 = 614.

items.q: 23 = 8?
items.e: Look at the numerators: 2 × 4 = 8. Multiply the denominator by 4 too: 3 × 4 = 12. So 23 = 812.

items.q: 34 = 9?
items.e: Look at the numerators: 3 × 3 = 9. Multiply the denominator by 3 too: 4 × 3 = 12. So 34 = 912.

items.q: 25 = 6?
items.e: Look at the numerators: 2 × 3 = 6. Multiply the denominator by 3 too: 5 × 3 = 15. So 25 = 615.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 34?
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number: 3 × 3 = 9 and 4 × 3 = 12. So 34 = 912. Multiplying only the numerator makes a bigger amount.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 25?
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number: 2 × 2 = 4 and 5 × 2 = 10. So 25 = 410. Multiplying only the numerator makes a bigger amount.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 56?
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number: 5 × 2 = 10 and 6 × 2 = 12. So 56 = 1012. Multiplying only the numerator makes a bigger amount.

items.q: Which fraction is not in the same family as 12?
items.e: 23 is not equal to 12: 1 was added to the numerator and the denominator of 12. The others are in the family, because both numbers were multiplied by the same number.

items.q: Which fraction is not in the same family as 13?
items.e: 34 is not equal to 13: 2 was added to the numerator and the denominator of 13. The others are in the family, because both numbers were multiplied by the same number.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. 54 are shaded. Write this as a mixed number.
items.e: 44 = 1 whole. One more quarter is shaded. So 54 = 1 14.

items.q: 74 = ?
items.e: 44 make 1 whole. 7 − 4 = 3 quarters are left over. So 74 = 1 34.

items.q: 1 23 = ?3
items.e: 1 whole = 33. Add the 2 thirds: 3 + 2 = 5. So 1 23 = 53.

items.q: Which improper fraction is equal to 2 12?
items.e: 2 wholes = 42. Add the half: 4 + 1 = 5 halves. So 2 12 = 52.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which fraction is greater?
items.e: Same denominator, so the parts are the same size. Compare the numerators: more parts is more. 58 > 38.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which fraction is greater?
items.e: Same numerator, so you have the same number of parts. A smaller denominator means bigger parts. 23 > 25.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which fraction is greater?
items.e: Same numerator, so you have the same number of parts. A smaller denominator means bigger parts. 34 > 310.

items.q: Compare. Choose <, > or =.
c: 46 < 56
46 = 56
46 > 56
items.e: Same denominator, so the parts are the same size. Compare the numerators: more parts is more. 56 > 46.

items.q: Which fraction is the greatest?
items.e: All the numerators are 3, so look at the denominators. The smallest denominator (4) gives the biggest parts. 34 is the greatest.

items.q: Which fraction is the least?
items.e: All the denominators are 8, so the parts are the same size. The smallest numerator is the least: 28.

items.q: Order from least to greatest: 13, 110, 15
c: 15, 13, 110
110, 15, 13
13, 15, 110
13, 110, 15
items.e: Same numerator. The biggest denominator is the smallest fraction, so start with 110. Least to greatest: 110, 15, 13.

items.q: Order from least to greatest: 24, 28, 26
c: 28, 26, 24
24, 26, 28
26, 28, 24
24, 28, 26
items.e: Same numerator, 2. Eighths are smaller than sixths, and sixths are smaller than fourths. Least to greatest: 28, 26, 24.

items.q: Order from greatest to least: 410, 910, 610
c: 910, 410, 610
610, 910, 410
910, 610, 410
410, 610, 910
items.e: Same denominator, so compare the numerators: 9 > 6 > 4. Greatest to least: 910, 610, 410.

items.q: Group A: 3 pizzas are shared equally by 4 friends. Group B: 3 pizzas are shared equally by 5 friends. In which group does each friend get more pizza?
items.e: Group A: each friend gets 34 of a pizza. Group B: each gets 35. Same numerator, and fewer sharers means bigger shares, so 34 > 35. Group A gets more.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Which improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is cut into 4 equal parts, so each part is 14. Count the shaded parts: 7. So it is 74. The denominator is the number of parts in one whole, not in all the bars.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Which improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is cut into 3 equal parts, so each part is 13. Count the shaded parts: 5. So it is 53. The denominator is the number of parts in one whole, not in all the bars.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Which improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is cut into 2 equal parts, so each part is 12. Count the shaded parts: 5. So it is 52. The denominator is the number of parts in one whole, not in all the bars.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Which improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each bar is cut into 5 equal parts, so each part is 15. Count the shaded parts: 8. So it is 85. The denominator is the number of parts in one whole, not in all the bars.

items.q: Each circle is 1 whole. Which improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each circle is cut into 4 equal parts, so each part is 14. Count the shaded parts: 9. So it is 94. The denominator is the number of parts in one whole, not in all the circles.

items.q: Each circle is 1 whole. Which improper fraction is shaded?
items.e: Each circle is cut into 3 equal parts, so each part is 13. Count the shaded parts: 7. So it is 73. The denominator is the number of parts in one whole, not in all the circles.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Which mixed number is shaded?
items.e: 2 bars are full, so that is 2 wholes. 3 quarters more are shaded. So it is 2 34 (= 114).

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Which mixed number is shaded?
items.e: 2 bars are full, so that is 2 wholes. 2 thirds more are shaded. So it is 2 23 (= 83).

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Which mixed number is shaded?
items.e: 1 bar is full, so that is 1 whole. 2 fifths more are shaded. So it is 1 25 (= 75).

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. Which mixed number is shaded?
items.e: 3 bars are full, so that is 3 wholes. 1 half more is shaded. So it is 3 12 (= 72).

items.q: There are 32 students in a Class 4. 38 of them have school dinners. How many students have school dinners?
items.e: First find 18: 32 ÷ 8 = 4 students. Then multiply by the numerator: 4 students × 3 = 12 students.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Zoya eats 38 of the pizza and Vivaan eats 28. What fraction of the pizza do they eat altogether?
items.e: The slices are all eighths. 3 + 2 = 5 eighths: 58. Keep the denominator 8.

items.q: Rahul has a ribbon 60 cm long. He uses 34 of it to make a bow. How long is the piece for the bow?
items.e: First find 14: 60 ÷ 4 = 15 cm. Then multiply by the numerator: 15 cm × 3 = 45 cm.

items.q: Priya has 910 m of ribbon. She uses 410 m for a card. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: 9 − 4 = 5 tenths. The denominator stays 10, so 510 m is left.

items.q: Fatima practises the piano for 34 of an hour. How many minutes is that?
items.e: There are 60 minutes in an hour (not 100). 60 ÷ 4 = 15, so 14 of an hour is 15 minutes. 15 × 3 = 45 minutes.

items.q: A book has 48 pages. Anika has read 56 of it. How many pages does she have left to read?
items.e: 56 of 48: 48 ÷ 6 = 8, so 56 is 8 × 5 = 40 pages read. 48 − 40 = 8 pages left. (Quicker: 16 is left, and 16 of 48 is 8.)

items.q: A nature trail is 1,000 m long. Kavya has walked 310 of it. How far has she walked?
items.e: First find 110: 1,000 ÷ 10 = 100 m. Then multiply by the numerator: 100 m × 3 = 300 m.

items.q: Tara has a bag of 24 sweets. 13 of them are red. How many red sweets are there?
items.e: To find 13, divide by the denominator: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 sweets.

items.q: A school car park has 60 spaces. 710 of the spaces are full. How many spaces are empty?
items.e: 710 of 60: 60 ÷ 10 = 6, and 6 × 7 = 42 spaces are full. 60 − 42 = 18 spaces are empty.

items.q: Varun eats 24 of a chocolate bar. Meera eats 48 of a bar of the same size. Who eats more?
items.e: Multiply the numerator and denominator of 24 by 2: 24 = 48. Meera eats more pieces, but they are smaller, so they eat the same amount.

items.q: Which multiplication is the same as 14 + 14 + 14?
items.e: 14 + 14 + 14 is 14 added 3 times. That is 3 groups of 14: 3 × 14.

items.q: 3 × 14 = ?
items.e: 3 × 14 means 14 + 14 + 14. Three fourths is 34. The parts are still fourths, so the denominator stays 4.

items.q: 5 × 18 = ?
items.e: 5 × 18 means 5 copies of 18: 5 eighths, or 58. Do not multiply the denominator.

items.q: Which addition is the same as 4 × 110?
c: 110 + 110 + 110
110 + 110 + 110 + 110
110 + 110 + 110 + 110 + 110
items.e: 4 × 110 means add 110 4 times: 110 + 110 + 110 + 110 = 410.

items.q: 6 × 14 = ?
items.e: 6 × 14 is 6 fourths, 64. 4 fourths make 1 whole, and 2 fourths are left. So it is 1 24.

items.q: 7 × 13 = ?
items.e: 7 × 13 is 7 thirds, 73. 6 thirds make 2 wholes, and 1 third is left. So it is 2 13.

items.q: ? × 15 = 45
items.e: 45 is 4 fifths, so you need 4 copies of 15: 4 × 15 = 45.

items.q: Zoya skates 14 of a lap around the rink, 3 times. How much of a lap does she skate in all?
items.e: 3 × 14 = 14 + 14 + 14 = 34 of a lap.

items.q: A hockey game has 3 periods of the same length. Rehan watches 2 periods. What fraction of the game does he watch?
items.e: The game has 3 equal parts, so the denominator is 3. He watches 2 of them: 23.

items.q: A tourtière is cut into 8 equal pieces. The family eats 5 pieces. What fraction of the tourtière do they eat?
items.e: There are 8 equal pieces, so the denominator is 8. They eat 5 pieces: 58.
